On the basis of this overview layout map, there were working maps that were made daily and which showed in detail the terrorist forces in their different concentrations and locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When was this particular one made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my recollection at this point, it was sometime around February 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know if we're looking at some sort of photographic representation of the original map or is this a map that has been subsequently reconstructed from material that was earlier available?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a photographic map -- realistic photographic representation from that particular period, and this was something that was regularly done in the Corps Command, such a way of representing the locations of the terrorist forces, namely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not sure that answers the question. Was this map constructed later, after these events were all over, from material that was available or is this a map which was actually in use in 1999, this particular one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map, to the best of my recollection, was created in February 1999 in order to monitor the growth of the forces of the armed rebellion and their preparation for what they termed "the spring offensive." To the best of my recollection, it was created and used in February 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] .

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, thank you. We have attempted to provide Their Honours with a picture of 1999 and what the Pristina Corps was facing at the time. I would now like to move on to deal with the Pristina Corps, the orders it issued and its activities in 1998. Please, first of all, explain to us the organisational structure, purposes and tasks of the Pristina Corps in 1998.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The Pristina Corps was the operative part of the 3rd Army of the Army of Yugoslavia, deployed in seven garrisons on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, plus one garrison outside Kosovo and Metohija. There were nine units of regiment or brigade rank, seven units of independent battalion rank, two company-level units, one installation. In peacetime, according to the establishment, it numbered 12.000, and in wartime, about 34.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What were the tasks of the Pristina Corps in 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The priority operative tasks were the following: To secure and defend the state border with Albania and Macedonia on a front that was 261 kilometres long; reinforced security of military facilities in Kosovo and Metohija, of which there were over 60; regular combat training of soldiers in the command units, and the fundamental tasks of any army in the world and of the Pristina Corps in peace was that. The fourth task was to secure the main roads, to make them passable in the corps area, especially towards the state border, and in one part of the year 1998, over a period of two to two and a half months, to provide support with some of our forces to the MUP forces in putting down rebellion and terrorism and armed rebellion on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. Those were the tasks of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General Perisic reported on that to the president of Yugoslavia. That's Exhibit 3D757; is that correct? Are you aware of this in relation to these tasks of the Pristina Corps in 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I know that from the evidence, but these were practically the tasks of the corps in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The tasks that were carried out?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: According to the Rules of Service of the Army of Yugoslavia from 1994, was the use of units and facilities of the Army of Yugoslavia in peacetime envisaged and prescribed for?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, through three or four paragraphs in the Rules of Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me assist you, General. We will now look at Exhibit -- excuse me -- P1085.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have in e-court K0367406. That's paragraph 2: "Use of units or facilities or installations in peacetime," and the paragraph is 447. In e-court, that's page 214. It's 214 in e-court, in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now that we have it on the screen now, General, can you comment on paragraph 47? Apart from its regular tasks, the regular tasks of the units and facilities, it says that the army can be used in peacetime for the following purposes. Can you please read out to us for what purposes?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The protection and rescue of people and the salvaging of property from natural disasters and other accidents; securing public roads and buildings of special significance for the defence of the country."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, here it is in English, for the sake of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please read a little more slowly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Securing public roads and installations of special significance for the defence of the country; maintaining order at large celebrations, ceremonies and parades; combatting insurgent, sabotage, terrorist and other hostile armed groups."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you pause here? We need not go on. According to the Rules of Service of the Army of Yugoslavia, in peacetime the Army of Yugoslavia may be used for the combat you just referred to.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, there's no doubt about that in the mind of any member of the army. This was how it was then, and it still is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, we've heard a lot of discussion here about whether the army can be used in this way or not, but let's proceed and comment on two more paragraphs. Can you look at paragraph 448, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, please look at paragraph 448.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do I need to read it or should I comment on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, we can read it for ourselves, so please just comment.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This paragraph regulates the following: To secure public roads and installations of special significance for the defence of the country, the decision and order for the use of army units is made by the army commander, not the chief of the General Staff; rather, it's the army commander in his own area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's see if the interpretation has finished. Could you now comment on paragraph 450? Could you please read it first.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Should I read it or explain it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, it's important and there's been quite a lot of discussion of it, so please first read it and then comment on it briefly.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Army units may be used to fight insurgent, sabotage, terrorist and other hostile armed groups or to prevent and eliminate a state of emergency in accordance with a decision of the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia ..." And then it goes on to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And can you finish reading --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: " ... Or the Defence Council."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now the next paragraph. It's important to analyse all this, so will you read the next paragraph as well.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The decision on the use of army units for carrying out tasks shall be issued by the chief of the General Staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And now, General, this last paragraph, can you read it slowly and then comment on it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "On the occasion of an attack by an insurgent, terrorist, sabotage or other hostile armed group on a unit or institution, the commanding officer of the attacked unit, institution or military installation, or the duty officer, shall immediately take the appropriate measures for defence and for repelling the attack and notify his superior." My comment, in brief, is as follows: There is no separate order to be issued for the defence of a unit from an attack on the unit or the facility. The immediate commanding officer immediately repels the attack and then informs his superior of what's going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And all this obtains in peacetime, and as we saw in the previous paragraph, before any kind of state of emergency or similar situation is declared?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This whole chapter, Chapter 6 and 7, refer to the use of the army in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, the first part of paragraph 450 refers to a decision of the president of the Supreme Defence Council. Now, in what circumstances do you envisage that the right of the army units to act depends on a decision of the president of the Supreme Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my understanding of this paragraph is as follows: It refers to the use of army units of the Army of Yugoslavia to suppress terrorism on certain territory belonging to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and in my assessment this would entail a serious threat to security, the security of the state, that is. In that case, the president of the FRY, based on a decision of the Supreme Defence Council, issues a decision with the chief of the General Staff, makes operational through his orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that not what Perisic was concerned about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my answer is, yes, Perisic, but as for the rest, I don't know how to respond as to what he was concerned about, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let me just check whether I understand you correctly, whether I read you correctly. It says that army units may be used in combat against insurgent, sabotage, terrorist and other hostile groups or to prevent and eliminate a state of emergency. If it is envisaged that they should be used in a fight against terrorism in order to prevent a state of emergency, does that mean they may be used without declaring a state of emergency?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As a citizen of the country, not to mention as a soldier, when I know that 50 per cent of the territory of the Province of Kosovo and Metohija is blocked by armed rebel forces, that is the most severe state of emergency that can exist in a country. And the fact that the state has not decided to declare a state of emergency is up to the state organs, but it doesn't affect the need to use army units to eliminate the threat. You asked me whether it can be used without having a state of war declared previously, but certainly, yes, the answer is "yes," because this paragraph says that no state of emergency is needed for the army to be used under the Rules of Service to carry out these tasks as defined here in the Rules of Service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think I understand that clearly, but this would suggest that two things are required before the army can be used to fight insurgent, sabotage or terrorist groups. First of all, the president of the Supreme Defence Council has to make a decision, and, secondly, the chief of the General Staff has to issue an order. Now, is it not that the authority for the action at all that concerned Perisic; in other words, he was concerned that this activity was being undertaken without an order from him or a decision of the president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, please don't take it amiss if some things that are at that level I cannot substantiate with facts. But my knowledge -- to my knowledge, the Supreme Defence Council did make a decision, but as a chief of staff in a corps in 1998, I did have the decision of my corps commander, and I want to tell you that for every day in 1998, the commander of the 3rd Army, General Samardzic, made the decision that concerned four levels of command downwards which was not in accordance with the doctrine, to use the corps units to this purpose, but I did not have any specific information and I was not in a position to see a decision up there in Belgrade or to have some other information down there in Djakovica, but I was able to see some of that in the evidence that was presented here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If, Your Honour, if you don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, Mr. President now asked you whether a decision had to be made by the chief of the General Staff. Did the chief of the General Staff issue any directive or any decision as to the use of forces in mid-1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. We had it here. I know that -- I knew that at the time, and I know that from this courtroom. That was Grom-98, 1 and 2, that was a directive issued by General Perisic about the use of the army in Kosovo and Metohija. In Chapter 1, he confirms the engagement or the use of the army up until that time, if that's what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, but let me just stop you here for an additional question. After this directive in July and August, you were at the forward command post at Djakovica. Did General Perisic, chief of the General Staff, spend any time at this focal point, the area where there were such strong -- those terrorist strongholds, did he have any direct insight into the situation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With the permission of the Honourable Trial Chamber, I would like to say that I have reliable information that there were more than 20 visits, inspections, carried out by large teams sent from the General Staff in 1998, and their focus was in Metohija. I know that the chief of the General Staff visited the areas at risk five times. I know that I personally reported to him in Djakovica about the threat to the state territory, and I know that dozens of times I, as the chief of Staff of the Corps, was called on a direct line from the General Staff by him. He asked me questions about the security situation in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me just clarify one more thing that stems from a question asked by Judge Bonomy. Units of the Army of Yugoslavia may be used to fight renegade, rebel and terrorist and other hostile forces. There is a comma there, and then it says: "... Or to prevent and eliminate the state of emergency according to the decision of the Supreme Defence Council or the president of the state." Is there an "or," or, rather, how am I supposed to read it? Is my reading wrong?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, in legal terms, I can't really tell you. There is some kind of a correlation there, but I think that I gave you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Fine. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, there may be significance in your point. The comma doesn't appear in the English version. Are you saying that there's a comma between "armed groups" and "or to prevent"? They're both on the screen, I think. You can tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is, there is a comma in the Serbian version. It's the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Riaz, could you go back also to paragraph 447, please, in the English. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I continue? I believe that this paragraph 447 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in the documents that we saw before the Court, the term "joint combat actions" was used quite often?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This term is used in the Rules of Combat of the Army of Yugoslavia, and manuals, such as the manual for the work of the Command and Staff, joint "objedinjena," combat operations, this means the direction -- directing and coordinating of a number of agents in the defence system within the framework of a single task. So it is a term that is broader than "coordination." Directing and coordinating the work of various agents within the framework of a certain task which can be a combat task or a non-combat task. So I'm talking about the way this term is used in manuals and Rules of Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the term used in the answer is "joint," and General Lazarevic used the term "objedinjena," which means "combined," and he also used the term "zajednicka," which can be translated as "joint," because as the transcript stands now, the term "joint" is used to cover both of these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there a difference?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, precisely. In order to clarify things for the transcript, I would like to ask General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The term "combined command" or, rather, "combined operations" and "joint operations," is there a difference?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there is a difference. When we're talking about combined operations, combat or other operations, this refers to the coordination of the actions between forces which are not subordinate to each other, which are not in the same chain of command, as is the term that we've been using in this trial, so there's no subordination. There is discussion, there is coordination, there is direction, or there is an effort to reach a consensus within the participants -- among the participants in the same task in a NATO parlance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that mean, for the avoidance of any doubt, that the word in B/C/S used for the Joint Command is the same word as you have been using here to describe joint operations? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the combat rules of the Army of Yugoslavia, quite specifically in the manual for the commands and staffs, this is one of the fundamental manuals for -- used in the work of the Army of Yugoslavia, defines the combined command quite specifically, or rather the combined command post, not joint command post but combined command post, where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The simple question I'm asking, the word used is "zajednicka" now, does that word appear in the expression "joint command," Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we're talking about "objedinjena" not "zajednicka." "Objedinjena" is combined, "zajednicka" is joint. Let me give you an example. For instance, we are all combined here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In the expression "the Joint Command" that we've been using throughout this trial, what is the B/C/S word for "joint"?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: "Zajednicka."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking you that and so that you can have an opportunity to explain it, if there is this distinction between combined and joint operations, and the word "joint" means that there is only one line of command because of resubordination, it's a very important point in the definition of what "Joint Command" means, and that's what I was trying to clarify. It's not a combined command, it's a joint command. Anyway, please proceed with your own examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I understand. Perhaps the best way to see the difference is if we use an example. Could we please have Exhibit 5D264. It's a very brief document, and perhaps you can just comment on it in light of this difference that we're trying to draw here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the 3rd Army Command that speaks about combining the operations of the ground forces, or to be quite specific the 3rd Army, and the Air Force in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Army by setting up special cooperation organs. So every structure in the 3rd Army and the Air Force Command have their executive command -- retain the executive command over their own units. This is a typical example of combining combat operations over a broader area. Area, in this case within the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it possible to combine the operations outside of the army? We saw that two different structures that have their own chains of command are combined. Is it possible to achieve this kind of combining outside of -- to involve structures other than the army?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Law on Defence deals with the issue of combining not only combat operations but other forms of armed and non-armed resistance, in terms of directing and coordinating the activities within the framework of a task, and I would like to ask the Presiding Judge to give me a minute to explain the difference between the -- to explain the difference when it comes to the Joint Command, because we did not go into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please do so, because I think that we have the permission of the Trial Chamber. I was going to come to that with other documents, but perhaps now is the good time.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am using the official terms here, the terms that are used in the combat rules, in the manuals of the army and in the Law on Defence, but in military parlance, in 1998 and even in 1999, there were commands -- commanding offices and officers who would use the term "combined" joint command of the military and the MUP. What I want to say is the term "zajednicka komandant" the "Joint Command," is not defined anywhere in the Rules, but they used this term for the combined command. This was done by some commands, by some officers. And there is evidence -- I don't know whether my Defence team will be able to locate that and to present it to the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, we were going to come to that. I didn't want to interrupt you. Your Honours, we will deal with that topic when the appropriate documents come up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I simply wanted to ask Mr. Lazarevic at this point: What are the official terms that he is referring to? In your answer there, Mr. Lazarevic, you said you were using the official terms here from the combat rules and manuals. Can you tell me which are the official terms that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The official terms, Your Honour, are "objedinjena komandno mesto," combined command post, combining combat operations, combining other forms of armed or non-armed resistance, so these are the official terms that are used, "objedinjena" and "objedinjena komandno mesto," combined command post, which for all intents and purposes is the "objedinjena komanda," or combined command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a suggestion for my colleagues who have a much better mastery of both the English and Serbian language. The suggestion is to use the term -- but perhaps the best idea would be for Mr. Ivetic to assist us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I don't think that is going to be of assistance, Mr. Bakrac. Just please continue with the questions. Submissions are something which can be made at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, well, perhaps through this document we might -- we might look at this issue through 5D424. There may be even some mistakes in translation. I would just like to invite General Lazarevic to read one sentence and for us to see how it was translated. So 5D424.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, now we have the English, too. Could you please tell us, just very briefly, what is this document, what is this all about? And then I will ask you to read just one sentence from it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the Supreme Command staff, from the Air Force and Air Defence Administration. It is the wartime period, the 15th of May, 1999. It is sent to the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what is the gist of this document, just very briefly? And then we will go on to read the part.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, the essence of this document is that a suggestion is made -- a proposal is made, how to coordinate and combine all the operations of the Army of Yugoslavia, in terms of anti-aircraft defence in Kosovo and Metohija during the war, that were placed under the command of two strategic groups, the 3rd Army and the Air Force and Air Defence Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And could you please read in the first sentence in paragraph two?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Your idea of the need to coordinate-combine the forces and the assets of the anti-aircraft defence according to task is indispensable."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not quite sure whether the sentence has been translated properly. "Your idea about the coordination-combination" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there is already a translation, as you know, and this is effectively the same, although the precise wording is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that the essence has been conveyed as it should have been, but perhaps now would be the best time to take a break so that we may resolve any translation and interpretation problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hannis, I've caused an investigation to be made into the translation issue, because my understanding, as of ten days ago or so, was that everything was to be translated in time for the commencement of the Defence case. Apparently there's been a misunderstanding about when that date was, and CLS were under the impression that the Defence would not commence until next Monday. As a result, a special effort is being made today and tomorrow to deal with the outstanding translations, so hopefully the matter will be resolved before the end of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll have a break now and resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, before we proceed, we looked at the transcript and we believe a thing needs clarification. Namely, here we gave two examples of the combining of forces of the Air Force and the anti-aircraft defence and of the forces of the 3rd Army. When there is a combined command post or a combined combat operations, when we are talking about combining, does each one of these entities retain its own chain of command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It absolutely does retain such a chain. And with permission from the Trial Chamber, I should like to explain. Throughout the war, at the forward command post of the 3rd Army, the general area of Pristina, which was at the command post of the Pristina Corps, there was simultaneously, contemporaneously, the forward command post of the Air Force, corps of the Air Force and the anti-aircraft defence. The commander of the army could not order that forward command post of the Air Force Corps to support him, to support the army forces. He could only ask, he could only require, he could only propose, and it was on the Air Force to decide whether to use its air forces in Kosovo and Metohija. And just another sentence. Also throughout the war, at the corps command post, there was a group of Air Force liaison officers to whom I could personally only submit a request for any kind of support, medical or transportation support, but could not order them to do anything. In fact, a squadron of medical corps helicopters for the evacuation of wounded -- of the wounded from the Pristina Corps could not be used at my orders, but this was done by the group of Air Force liaison officers. This is combining activities in war, in armed struggle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Tell us now, on the basis of what were activities coordinated of the Army of Yugoslavia, i.e., the Pristina Corps and the MUP forces on tasks of suppressing terrorism and the armed rebellion in the second half of 1998.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This coordination of activities was defined by special plans from the group of the Grom-98 plan as well as by special orders which were issued by the General Staff, i.e., the 3rd Army Command, pursuant to a decision taken at the highest state level, the highest political and military state level.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For these tasks of the Pristina Corps, how much of its effectives did the Pristina Corps engage?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the period from the end of July to the end of September, the Pristina Corps engaged between 2 to a maximum of 10 per cent of its effectives to support MUP forces in suppressing terrorism and the armed rebellion. The other forces were engaged on those tasks that we discussed at the previous session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your question, Mr. Bakrac, related to the second half of 1998. Did you mean by that to confine it to the period July until September?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I probably misspoke, Your Honours. In 1998, from June, when the -- rather July, when the command post was set up, and -- from June, when the command post was set up, i.e., from July, when the decision on the Grom plan was adopted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I comment on this and give a new response?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. The answer relates to the period of July to September. My question is whether you meant to confine the matter to that period, and you may have done, but can you clarify that for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we spoke about this combined command post a while ago. Are you familiar with the American rule FM3? It speaks about the lack of command powers and what is to be done in such situation. Are you familiar with it and can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm certainly familiar with it. This is a doctrinary rule for the use of the ground forces of the United States of America and, thereby, also of the NATO alliance, and to the best of my recollection, at this time it is item 445, I believe. I didn't delve deep into the rule. It is written in conditions when there is no command subordination, i.e., chain of command, the commanders of different units, of different formations, harmonise their activities, coordinate their activities, and negotiate it, and as it is put, arrive at a consensus how best to conduct their general task whereby each command and each unit retains the command function over its own forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in which way was this combining of combat operations of the Army of Yugoslavia, of the Yugoslav Army and the units of the Ministry of the Interior, carried out in 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The entire set of activities falls within this combining and coordination of the activities of the army and the police during 1998, and that is, first and foremost, exchange of intelligence data, exchange of information on the engagement and tasks of units in a certain specific area; thirdly, exchange of information on communications and communications equipment in order to be compatible, and then the assigning of representatives, or as is army parlance, liaison officers, to a certain MUP unit and vice versa, from the army and vice versa. And then during an action, there is set up, conditionally speaking, a combined command post, and plans are elaborated of combined operations and concerted action.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did the Command of the 3rd Army and the Pristina Corps prepare plans of concerted action and cooperation to support forces of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Neither did the 3rd Army prepare, and I do know that the Pristina Corps certainly did not prepare any such plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In view of the absence of the fact that there did not exist any general concerted action plans, how was the issue addressed of coordination?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that the Corps Command, in its combat documents, in its orders, in its commands, in its decisions and other documents, in a certain item which is envisaged according to the rules for that particular purpose, regulated concerted action with MUP forces. And in a certain specific document, the Corps Command, in that particular item, which often as a rule was the 13th item in combat documents, inserted a clause to the effect that the commanding forces of the army and of the MUP shall be conducted and combined by the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, while we are on this subject, can we move on to Prosecution document 5D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the number of the document for the interpreter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you repeat the number, please, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. P1428. Yes, perhaps I spoke too fast. Because it has been opened so many times, that's why I did so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I expect that you recognise this document. The heading states -- can you comment on it? It says: "The Command of the Pristina Corps." It has a strictly confidential number. The date is the 14th of August, 1998, and it is a decision on breaking up DTS forces in the sector of the Slup and Voksa villages. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this document. I signed it on behalf of the corps commander who on that date was with the chief of the General Staff, General Perisic inspecting the units, and this is an abridged order or command, or rather, as it is written here, a decision on breaking up sabotage and terrorist forces in the Slup and Voksa sector. It states that part of the forces, specifically the 15th-3 Combat Groups, should support the MUP forces in breaking up terrorist forces in the area of the Slup and Voksa villages, as evident in item 2.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, who brought this decision and who approved this decision?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The decision for the execution of this task was adopted by, first, the commander of the 3rd Army, General Samardzic, in his combat report, and he informed the chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, General Perisic, of his decision. Following that decision, the commander of the Pristina Corps, General Pavkovic, adopted -- issued a decision on a map which was signed and verified by the commander of the 3rd Army, Samardzic. That map is an attachment to this decision or abridged command order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let us not open Exhibit 5D1174. That is a regular combat report of the -- from the forward command post of the 3rd Army of the 14th of August, 1998, which contains the decision of General Samardzic, and this is something which has already been opened in respect to General Simic. But if you feel that it should be brought up on the screen, then we will do so. Should we open it or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's a matter for you, Mr. Bakrac. I don't see the need for it, but you have to decide how you present your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. I actually meant what I said for the sake of Your Honours, but the exhibit number of the map with this decision is 5D1175. Can we please have this map brought up on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we are waiting for the map on the e-court, there is an intervention on the transcript, page 70, lines 5 and 6. I believe the witness says: "I signed it on behalf of the corps commander who on that date was accompanying General Perisic inspecting the units."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That makes sense. Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, colleague Zecevic. We wanted to intervene ourselves. Could we see the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, is this the map decision for Voksa, and does it refer to this document that you signed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the map decision prepared by the corps commander, General Pavkovic, and endorsed by the commander of the 3rd Army, General Samardzic, approved for the specific action. We saw the decision for that particular action a while ago in written form.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And this map was attached to that decision, if I got it right.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you understood it properly. That was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But I have nevertheless decided that we see, in order to clarify matters, Exhibit 5D1174 on our screens. General, you have before you the daily combat report of the forward command post of the 3rd Army, addressed to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please look at point 5 or item 5. It's on the third page. Item 5. Could you please read item 5 and explain what it means?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Item 5 is a decision by the Command of the 3rd Army, and in the executive sense it says: "I have decided to continue providing increased security on the state border, with focus on the axes leading over the Junik mountains in order to prevent raids by terrorist forces, and the bringing in of weapons and military equipment to the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, with Combat Group 15-3, support MUP forces in crushing sabotage terrorist strong holds in the following sectors, Grabovac, Loja, Raui and Voksa." I think the rest is immaterial.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, I think there's no need to go to e-court. What I'd like to know is the following: This method of planning and issuing decisions concerning an action, is it a legitimate, lawful manner of doing so within the chain of command of the army, what we have just seen, that is?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes. And by Their Honours' leave, I would like to say that at the strategic level, it is unusual for an army commander to issue a decision for a combat group which numbered 197 men at the time to be included in the carrying out of a combat task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, why does it say, in item 6, that the Joint Command for KiM will be in command of this action from the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I started explaining the documents of the Corps Command of 1998 in which cooperation and coordinated action with MUP forces was described. As there was a lack of concrete, specific plans for cooperation and coordination, which should have been done according to the Rules of Combat, the Corps Command decided, in the last item which is dedicated to cooperation and coordination, to use this expression in order to indicate that the action would be of common interest, of joint interest, and that cooperation and coordination would be in place between the army and the MUP and their forces. So my explanation to you and Their Honours is that because there was a lack of cooperation and coordination plans, the Corps Command decided to use this clause; and I have to explain to Their Honours that this is a bit unusual and it's been confusing all of us for a year and a half. But that's what I know from that period of time, and that is the explanation I can give at present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We don't seem to have item 6 in English on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise. It may have been my error. I went back to document P14. That's the one I'm referring to now, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we see it and, please, item 6 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let's simplify matters even further. You say here: "Combat operations will be commanded by the Joint Command for KiM from the forward command post in Djakovica." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: At that time, were you at the forward command post in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was at the forward command post in Djakovica, and at that time, in the office in which I spent several months, there was a team from the General Staff, headed by General Obradovic, who testified here on that day and thereabouts, in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And it says here that combat operations will be commanded by the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija from that office; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In that office, in the course of these combat operations, were any of the following people present: Minic, Andjelkovic, Sainovic, Matkovic, or any other civilian?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, not a single one of those mentioned. There was a forward command post. That was a group of some ten officers. And on the ground, there was a command. I can't remember of what police detachment, which, in coordinated action with Group 15-3, that's a combat group from the 15th Armoured Brigade, carried out this task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I just clarify one thing with you. You've explained to us why this expression "commanded by the Joint Command for Kosovo" was used. Am I correct in understanding that it's a pure coincidence that that expression occurs in this document, used by you, and occurs in so many other documents? The two are not in any way related to each other; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not sure I understood your question properly, but I'll attempt to answer. This is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't want you to misunderstand. You have said that your explanation to us, as you called us "Their Honours," for the use of this word, this expression, was that because there was a lack of cooperation and coordination plans, the Corps Command decided to use this clause. Now, have I wrongly understood that you were talking about using it only in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only in this document, no. There were several such documents issued in the course of 1998, but this expression was used only and exclusively when there was a need to have cooperation, a coordinated action, and mutual support between the army and the police. It was used only in such cases where these forces had to be combined, and that's where the term "joint command" was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That would suggest that you can tell us who originally decided to use that expression and when that was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with the best will in the world, I really don't know who, in the Corps Command, issued such a decision for the use of this term, because as of April, I was at the forward command post. I did, however, receive a number of documents containing this clause or expression, and as you can see, the operative organs of the Corps Command prepared these documents, and I prepared them on behalf of the Corps Command. But I cannot say with certainty when this term began to be used. All I know is that it refers to activities where there was a need for cooperation, coordinated action and support between the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I also have a question, General, kindly. In regard to your statement, when you said that for one and a half years there was a confusion about the different clauses of the documents, and then you thought or somebody thought in the court to use -- to invoke the words "cooperation for purposes of carrying forward the thing," please tell me, why didn't you seek a clarification about this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've obviously understood you differently, I think. You better explain to Judge Chowhan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may assist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... The period of the trial to date and not a previous period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: But even if we don't -- I apologise bothering you, but even if we don't talk one and a half and it was based on my confusion, but yet a clarification could have been sought.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are right to put such a question to me from the Bench, but I confess that this term is not present in the combat documents and the Rules of Combat. However, when at the forward command post, as the chief of Staff, I received a document from my commander, the commander of the Pristina Corps Command, and when I knew that the state top leadership had issued a decision that the army, with part of its forces, should support the MUP forces in suppressing an armed rebellion, and with all the knowledge I had as an officer, what I understood by this was that the army and the police were carrying out a task together to defend the integrity of the state. I had no doubts about that, no dilemmas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now that we are dealing with this topic, please take a look at Exhibit 6D731. General, do you recognise this document, and can you comment first on item 2, the first and second paragraphs of item 2, and then we'll proceed further.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Based -- or rather pursuant to the previous decision of the Command of the Pristina Corps for this action, which I signed, the commander of the 15th Armoured Brigade issued his own order for the engagement of Combat Group 3 to support MUP forces in a coordinated action, I'm explaining now, to carry out that task in Voksa on the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Could you comment on the last page, item 7, "Command and Communications." That's on the last page, the last two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 15th Armoured Brigade received a decision from the Corps in which, in item 6, it says that all forces would be commanded by the Joint Command from the forward command post in Djakovica, and he understood this properly, of course, and ordered that all forces carrying out the combat actions should be under the command and control of the Pristina Corps Command from the forward command post. Therefore, in the view of the brigade commander, there is no joint command. He understands quite properly that he is to be commanded by the Command of the Corps which is located in Djakovica from the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you comment on the previous paragraph as well, "Coordinated Action with Organs"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is a response to the questions put previously as to how coordinated action between the army and the MUP is organised. So he's ordering Combat Group 3 concerning preparing and executing combat activities, to maintain coordination before and in the course of carrying out the combat task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I understand correctly, that's an organisation of a coordinated action at a lower level.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at a lower tactical level. The group numbered 197 men, this combat group, and the police detachment was not much bigger, so that amounted to about four [as interpreted] battalions in size.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Between a company and a battalion, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 5D99.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honours. 78.23, I believe the witness said it was somewhere between -- between company and battalion in size. It says -- the transcript says "four battalions in size."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you clarify that, please, Mr. Lazarevic? What was the reference you made to battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said that the Combat Group 15-3 numbered about 200 men at the time. That was a company-strength unit. And the police detachment was a battalion-strength unit. I don't know their exact strength. But what I wanted to say is that the coordination at the lower tactical level, at the level between a company and a battalion, and that's what I said. So now I'm just providing some further explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It had actually been clarified. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we see how this was taken at the lower tactical level. Now have you in front of you document 5D99. This is a document, minutes of a meeting between the army command organs at the forward command post and commanders of subordinated units. The date is the 17th of August, 1998. Could we please move to page 2 now. Could you please read the paragraph right in the middle which begins with the words: "The PRK commander reports ..."?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The commander of the Pristina Corps reports on the daily activities of the units in which the MUP was supported by the 15-3 combat group, taking the villages of Jasic and Djocaj, where no casualties were sustained on our side."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, does this refer to those actions, the actions that we were talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This completed the circle in the execution of this task. From the army commander to the General Staff, down to the combat group, and now again the Pristina Corps commander informs the 3rd Army commander, General Samardzic, that the task had been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I just want to know -- I don't know if you know that. If you don't, just tell me so. Did the 3rd Army commander use the term "joint command"? Were you in a position to hear it on any occasion? But, please, do tell us if you didn't.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I did not attend a single meeting at the forward command post of the 3rd Army in Pristina. The 3rd Army commander did visit the Pristina Corps forward command post, where I was several times, but I never heard him use this term. I was in a position to see some documents here at this trial where he used this term.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But you don't know that he used them at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, units of the Pristina Corps, were they able to provide support to the Minister of Interior units in the field of their own volition without an order of their superior command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. The use of a unit -- a unit may be used without approval only if that unit or the facility it is securing come under an attack. In any other circumstances, permission should be sought from the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 4D377 up on the screen, Exhibit 4D377. It's a short document, and it does have a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please just read paragraph 4 and comment on it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is an order from the 3rd Army commander, General Samardzic, dated the 29th of May, 1998. In paragraph 4, he orders, quite specifically in no uncertain terms, that the support for the MUP forces should be done from the deployment sector of the units, using combat equipment from a distance, in line with its specifications; provide support only following a specific request from the commander of all the MUP forces at the Kosovo and Metohija pursuant to a decision from the chief of Staff of the 3rd Army Command and the Command of the Pristina Corps. And if you allow me, I would just like to say that there was no overall commander, but I understand this. This is what I was telling you. The 3rd Army commander quite resolutely stated that no element of the army could be used without his permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And we were able to see, in previous examples, Prosecution exhibits, that such orders were carried out very strictly and only on the orders and permission of the superior command within a legal chain of command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Every day, for every action, with the approval of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We were talking about the tasks of the Pristina Corps. I want to know the following: You were at the Djakovica forward command post. What was the purpose -- what were the tasks of the forward command post at Djakovica in 1998 at the time when you were there at that command post?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The setting up of the Pristina Corps forward command post in Djakovica, in April 1998, was ordered personally by the 3rd Army commander. He personally ordered that I, as the chief of Staff, should be there at the forward command post. The purpose was to coordinate the actions of the forces of the Pristina Corps and the 3rd Army in securing and defending the state border primarily facing Albania, and preventing the spill-over of terrorist activities from Albania into Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at Exhibit 4D380. And, just very briefly, could we see who issued the order for your appointment, who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And is this, in fact, the order for your appointment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is an order from the 3rd Army commander. The date is the 20th of April. In paragraph 2, he orders that the chief of Staff of the Corps should lead the forward command post, and the next day, I and a group of officers from the Corps Command, we took up the forward command post, and I remained there throughout 1998. So I was in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, the 3rd Army commander, General Samardzic, sent you there and he, indeed, signed this order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he ordered this, but I was sent there by the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Could you tell us, very briefly, something about the scope of your activities? We saw this action where support was provided to the MUP. We saw when you manned the forward command post. What was the focus of your activities in 1998 in the carrying out of your duties at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The forward command post of the Pristina Corps had a priority function, which was the following: From a distance of about 10 to 15 kilometres from the state border which was at risk, to monitor the security situation at the state border and the integrity of the state in this area, on a daily basis to visit and control the units, to coordinate their activities, to report to the Corps Command about any measures taken, to report, if necessary, directly to the army commander and the Chief of General Staff, and I would like to stress this because this was not in line with the usual military procedure, but I have to say that I was quite happy to receive a direct call from the chief of the General Staff or the army commander, inquiring about the security at the state border. So these were our priority tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, General. Your Honour, I see that I have two more minutes, and I would like to move on to a very interesting topic about some meetings in Pristina, so perhaps it would be a good idea to leave that for the morning, when we are all fresh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac, a suitable time to interrupt. Mr. Lazarevic, you're well aware now of the routine for witnesses. That's the category you now fall into, and therefore any discussion of the evidence in this case with anybody is absolutely off limits for you. And it may be harder for you than others because you can't necessarily distance yourself so easily from people who have an interest in the case, but the rule is just as strict for you as anyone else. You must discuss things other than the evidence in this case. We shall resume tomorrow at 9.00. Sorry, yes, in Courtroom number III and not in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
